newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST-Taiwan May M2 seen up 9.438 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Taiwan May M2 seen up 9.438 pct yr/yr.

text.p: A Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists on Monday projected an average 9.438 percent year-on-year rise in May for Taiwan's broadest money supply measure, M2.
Taiwan's monthly money supply figures were to be released by the central bank after 0400 GMT on June 25.
M2 growth in April was reported at 9.76 percent year-on-year.

Economists said they expected May M2 growth to fall into the central bank's target zone of 9-14 percent growth for the fifth straight month since the central bank adopted a new, broader definition of M2 in January.
They estimated the new definition was adding one to 1.5 percentage points to the closely watched indicator. Before the shift, it had been 16 months since M2 growth had hit target.

Economists said they expected slowing M2 growth in May, reflecting the central bank's unusually high issuance of short term negotiable certificates of deposit as well as some tightening of liquidity at the peak the state treasury's annual income tax collection.

"Liquidity tightened in May as the central bank continued to issue negotiable certificates of deposit and payments of some T$20-30 billion of income tax were made to the state treasury," said HSBC James Capel economist Stephen Wang.
National Securities economist Lin Kuo-yang said growth of bank loan approvals had continued to be sluggish, reflecting the general slowness of Taiwan's economic recovery.
